Humanoid (Planetouched) · 1 hex · SM +0 Aasimar [Monsters on Automatic, SRD coverage: humanoid folk and their sub-races; answers Aasimar (SRD 3.5)]

Somebody with a celestial somewhere back up the family line, and the descent shows: the eyes are wrong in a way nobody can place, and the hair holds light it was not given. Aasimar tend to end up doing the errand nobody else would take, partly out of conviction and partly because everyone assumes they will. Acid, cold and lightning all find them harder going than they should.

Notes

  • GCS ancestry draft: gcs/aasimar.gct
  • Independent build total: 98 points of racial traits plus 16 points of racial skills.
  • Answers the SRD heading(s): Aasimar (SRD 3.5). Only the creature identity is taken from the SRD; the GURPS statistics, ratings and prose are this project's own work and reproduce no SRD text.
  • Typical Stats, damage and ratings are derived from the racial template, not authored beside it, so the sheet and the stat block cannot disagree.
  • Body mass used to scale this build: 70 kg. ST, Size Modifier and DR are checked against it; see the gurps-animal-sanity-check skill for the bands.
  • Movement: ground Move 5 (primary). The published Move is the primary medium's cruising Move; sprint figures are stated here and not folded into it.
  • Treasure and grappling are not authored for this batch and ship as explicit nulls; `lair` carries a short habitat note, because where a wandering animal dens is an encounter fact rather than a loot one.
  • 1.8 m standing, which is the SM 0 row.
  • ST 10: an aasimar is a person, and nothing about the descent makes one stronger than the human it mostly is.
  • The inherited resistances are built as heavily Limited Damage Resistance, one damage type each, which is why they price into the template but do not raise the record's published DR. An aasimar is not armoured against a sword.
  • The daylight it can call once a day is not built as an attack: it lights a room, it does not injure anyone, and the rating path has no term for it. A GM should simply rule it.
